To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

free radicals alter intracytoplasmic ionic calcium levels, and membrane phospholipsids in cultured rat myocytes. alpha-Tocopheryl acetate prevents the alterations in ionic calcium and membrane phospholiplids.

the free radical generating system altered intracellular Ca levels, membrane phospholipid composition and morphology, and lactate-dehydrogenase release in cultured rat ventricle myocytes. alpha-Tocopheryl acetate attenuated these alterations.

exposure of cultured rat ventricular cells to free radical generating systems resulted in an increase in intracellular calcium levels and membrane damage, as evidenced by the development of blebs and increased release of lactate dehydroganese. alpha-Tocophorol, when added prior to exposure of the cells to the free radical system, prevented both the increase in intracellular Ca++ and membrane damage.

the effects of reactive oxygen intermediates on myocardial cells in culture.
the effects of free radicals and alpha-tocopherols on the myocardium.
the effects of free radicals on intracellular Ca2+ levels and membrane phosphatidylcholine in cultured ventricular myocytes and the ability of alpha-tocoherol to prevent these effects.
